chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Quitting Jacquet over money in September 1948
summary: A pay controversy with Jacquet, partly his own headstrong youth, makes him leave and return to Washington.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Of course, after Jo left, for some reason.... I hope I'm not getting ahead of myself in this situation... Anyway, I think Jo stayed there until I left, and I left in 1948 -- I think it was another September that I left. And it had to do with a little controversy again that had to do with the money situation. But this time, it was something that could have been remedied, I think. It was just the idea that I was pretty young then, and headstrong a lot of times, and it came into a controversy that Illinois and I had, and I just up and quit, and left the band, and came back to Washington.
I think that sort of ended another segment or another period of the saga of John Malachi in this music world that I've been in for so long.
